elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: Grant now reads "grants to Licensee and its Affiliates, upon written notice to Licensor, a non-exclusive license"; "AFFILIATE" is a defined term (1.1) and "Licensee" is defined as the single named entity, so the extension adds real coverage rather than duplicating it.

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: Restriction (e) still bars use or access "by any individuals other than the employees of the Licensee and its Affiliates"; no contractor/agent language was added. To meet this element the grant and (e) would need "and contractors acting on Licensee's behalf".
The grant remains conditional on continuing payment ("provided that Licensee makes payments to Licensor as required under this Agreement") and no perpetuity language was inserted.
The word "irrevocable" does not appear; the licence remains subject to automatic termination on a non-carved-out Change of Control under Article XX.

elements.element: A subscription licence is terminable only for uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: Article XX retains automatic termination on any Change of Control (other than the new M&A carve-out) without any breach, so termination is not limited to uncured material breach.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to Customer's successors.
elements.evidence: Section 13.4(c) still requires Licensor's prior written consent for any assignment or transfer of licence rights that is not a Change of Control; only Change-of-Control M&A successors benefit from the new carve-out, so general successor transferability is not achieved.

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
elements.evidence: Operative grant: "grants to Licensee and its Affiliates, upon written notice to Licensor"; the conforming edit to restriction (e) removes the otherwise directly contradictory limit to "employees of the Licensee" only.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.
elements.evidence: Article XX now excepts "a merger or acquisition in which this Agreement and Licensee's rights and licenses hereunder are transferred to Licensee's successor without Licensor's approval" from automatic termination, and 13.4(c) expressly routes any Change of Control to Article XX "and not the provisions of this Section", so the consent/void mechanic in 13.4(c) does not bite on such a transfer.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: affiliates are covered on written notice in the operative grant, and an M&A successor transfer is expressly carved out of the Change of Control auto-termination, with 13.4(c) already deferring all Change-of-Control matters to Article XX so no contradictory retained sentence survives.

The conforming edit to restriction (e) is justified rather than surplus: the retained text limited access to "employees of the Licensee" and would have expressly contradicted the new Affiliate grant; nothing outside the two fallback elements was deleted or added (no survival tails, expense or procedure language).

Preferred level fails on four elements: no contractor coverage, no perpetual/irrevocable language for paid-up licences, no limitation of termination to uncured material breach, and no general successor transferability outside a Change of Control.

Drafting improvement (not a defect at the fallback level): the carve-out is phrased as an exception to termination ("transferred to Licensee's successor without Licensor's approval") rather than an affirmative permission. Consider adding a short direct permission in Article XX, e.g. "Licensee may transfer this Agreement and its licences to a successor in a merger or acquisition without Licensor's approval", to remove any circularity argument.

No new assignment exception was granted to Licensor, and Licensor's consent regime for all other Changes of Control (including the competitor/adverse-interest deeming language) survives intact; "Affiliates" uses the existing Section 1.1 definition, so no undefined term or dangling cross-reference is created.
